Validation and reproduction of published results

Source: vignettes/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd
library(DesignComplexSurvival)

The results of the package are checked in three ways:

  • the unit tests (tests/testthat/) compare the results with an independent Python implementation (inst/validation/python/, using matrix exponentials and adaptive quadrature) and, when the packages are installed, with gsDesign, gsDesign2, rpact and lrstat;
  • the scripts in inst/reproduce/ recompute sample sizes, numbers of events, analysis times, bounds and powers printed in articles and a statistical analysis plan;
  • the scripts in inst/validation/ compare the package with patient-level simulations, with the package PWEALL and with the decisions of lrstat::fseqbon().

The last two folders are run by their run_all.R, which judges every value as PASS (the criterion is met), EXPLAINED (the criterion is met after a registered explanation, such as an apparent misprint), FAIL, or INFO (not judged: a published value computed by a method that the package does not reproduce, or an asymptotic approximation compared with simulation). The results are installed with the package, and this article reads them:

judgements <- c("PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL", "INFO")
read_results <- function(folder) {
  utils::read.csv(system.file(folder, "results", "summary.csv",
                              package = "DesignComplexSurvival"))
}
rp <- read_results("reproduce")
vd <- read_results("validation")
count <- function(x, by) {
  tab <- as.data.frame.matrix(table(x[[by]], factor(x$judgement, levels = judgements)))
  tab$Total <- rowSums(tab)
  tab
}

Reproduction of published results

The scripts recompute 527 printed values from 16 sources. Each value has a criterion that reflects the rounding of the printed value, for example rounding up for a sample size or agreement to the printed digits for a power.

knitr::kable(count(rp, "source"))
PASS EXPLAINED FAIL INFO Total
Barthel2006 44 1 0 0 45
Erdmann2025 8 0 0 33 41
Glimm2010 20 3 0 0 23
Lakatos1988 2 0 0 16 18
Lakatos2002 0 0 0 16 16
Lu2021 19 1 0 24 44
Luo2019 29 15 0 4 48
MaurerBretz2013 11 4 0 0 15
Porcher2002 30 5 0 24 59
Shih1995 11 5 0 4 20
Sugimoto2017 3 18 0 9 30
Tamhane2010 68 10 0 0 78
Tang2022 0 16 0 0 16
TorresSaavedra2026 3 0 0 0 3
Vergote2024 9 1 0 6 16
Xia2016 0 0 0 55 55

In total 257 values pass, 79 are explained, 0 fail and 191 are not judged. The sources, criteria and registered explanations are listed in the README.md and explained.csv of inst/reproduce/.

Comparison with simulations and other software 

labels <- c(fastsurvival = "FastSurvival simulation",
            python = "Python simulation",
            python_two = "Python simulation, PFS and OS together",
            python_calendar = "Python simulation, switching from a calendar time",
            danzer = "Estimator of Danzer et al. (2025)",
            pweall = "PWEALL",
            lrstat_fseqbon = "lrstat::fseqbon()")
tab <- count(vd, "source")
n_scen <- tapply(vd$scenario, vd$source, function(x) length(unique(x)))
tab <- cbind(Route = ifelse(is.na(labels[rownames(tab)]), rownames(tab),
                            labels[rownames(tab)]),
             Scenarios = as.vector(n_scen[rownames(tab)]), tab)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE)
Route Scenarios PASS EXPLAINED FAIL INFO Total
Estimator of Danzer et al. (2025) 2 0 0 0 8 8
FastSurvival simulation 5 300 0 0 448 748
lrstat::fseqbon() 3 142 0 0 0 142
PWEALL 8 161 0 0 0 161
Python simulation 5 468 0 0 650 1118
Python simulation, switching from a calendar time 3 72 0 0 150 222
Python simulation, PFS and OS together 6 174 0 0 872 1046

The quantities with exact counterparts in the package (expected numbers of events and dropouts by group at calendar times, state occupation probabilities, survival functions, bounds, the per-patient covariances of the statistics, and the quantities of PWEALL and lrstat) are judged. The criteria are 4se (within 4 Monte Carlo standard errors), 4se_p (within 4 standard errors computed from the package value), and abs:x or rel:x (absolute or relative difference at most x):

judged <- vd[vd$judgement != "INFO", ]
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(criterion = judged$criterion,
                                 judgement = judged$judgement)))
criterion judgement Freq
4se PASS 396
4se_p PASS 568
abs:0.002 PASS 46
abs:1e-4 PASS 12
abs:1e-5 PASS 22
abs:1e-6 PASS 146
rel:0.002 PASS 115
rel:1e-6 PASS 12

In total 1,317 values pass and 0 fail.

The mean, standard deviation and correlation of the log-rank statistics, the power and the type I error are asymptotic approximations and are recorded as INFO with the difference in units of the standard error:

info <- vd[vd$judgement == "INFO" & is.finite(vd$se_used) & vd$se_used > 0, ]
z <- info$diff / info$se_used
hist(z, breaks = 40, main = "", xlab = "(simulation - package) / standard error")

Of the 2,084 INFO rows with a standard error, 1,672 are within 2 standard errors and 82 differ by more than 4. These rows, by quantity and by the approximation compared (column variant), and the ten largest differences:

big <- info[abs(z) > 4, ]
big$variant[big$variant == ""] <- "(none)"
table(quantity = big$quantity)
#> quantity
#>   dropouts     events     reject reject_any       time          z     z_corr 
#>          2         14          1          1          4         45         15
sort(table(variant = big$variant), decreasing = TRUE)
#> variant
#>       sd;variance=alternative                        (none) 
#>                            29                            18 
#>               mean=schoenfeld                 variance=null 
#>                            14                            10 
#>          variance=alternative     at the expected look time 
#>                             6                             2 
#>                   mean=direct mean=schoenfeld;variance=null 
#>                             1                             1 
#>              sd;variance=null 
#>                             1
big$z <- big$diff / big$se_used
head(big[order(-abs(big$z)), c("source", "scenario", "hypothesis", "quantity",
                               "endpoint", "variant", "simulated", "package", "z")], 10)

The standard deviation of the statistic with variance = "alternative" does not include the variability of the estimated variance (see vignette("group-sequential")), and the Schoenfeld approximation of the mean (mean = "schoenfeld") is less accurate when the hazard ratio changes over time, as in V2 (see the introductory article, vignette("DesignComplexSurvival")).

Type I error with unequal allocation

In the simulations, the rejection rate under the null hypothesis of the design with 2:1 allocation and looks at 75 and 150 deaths was above the nominal level. Larger simulations showed that this comes from the skewness of the log-rank statistic with unequal allocation and few events (see the last section of vignette("group-sequential")).

Rerunning the checks

FastSurvival, PWEALL and lrstat (0.3.4 or later) are needed only to rerun inst/validation/. The README.md of each folder describes how to run the scripts, the criteria and the files. Every compared value is listed with its judgment in results/summary.csv, and results/summary.md summarizes the results.

References

Danzer MF, Rufibach K, Beyersmann J, Schmidt R (2025). Exhausting the type I error level in event-driven group-sequential designs with a closed testing procedure for progression-free and overall survival. arXiv:2512.08658.
